9.text: the Russian authorities were under the impression that in dealing with the

10.text: Chukchee the utmost caution and prudence are required. This idea has been

11.text: retained up to quite recent times. I have spoken before of the Anui-fair riot

12.text: of 1895, the details of which are so characteristic. Another interesting incident

13.text: happened ten years before, in 1884. A Russian creole of Nishne-Kolymsk,

14.text: Semen Drushinin, while on a trading-trip to Cape Erri, had some difficulties

15.text: with the Maritime Chukchee of that place about a seal-carcass that was offered

16.text: for sale. He paid a “false price” for it, and the seal was taken back from

18.text: of Yakutsk would come to the Kolyma in order to punish the Chukchee, for

36.text: CHIEF OFFICERS OF THE ANADYR. — The Anadyr country, after the

37.text: abolishment of the fortress in 1764, had no officials, and was governed from

38.text: Gishiginsk. The first official was appointed in 1889, at the time of the

39.text: opening of the steamship-line from Vladivostok to Mariinsky Post once a year.
